frozen_question: Can Cairo CG 53465-53469, and especially CG 53469, be connected by excavation provenance, catalogue identity, inscription and object morphology to a Mendes Osirian phallus relic rather than merely to the burial equipment of a Mendes priest?

method_execution.TOPA_SPIDER: contemporary excavation notice -> modern museum provenance -> scholarly index -> object-level catalogue hunt
method_execution.FIVE_D_SPIRAL: findspot -> owner/priesthood -> catalogue group -> material/object ontology -> mythic/relic claim -> return to primary catalogue
method_execution.BEETLE_GRAZER: Met and derivative antiquities-market repetitions counted as one museum-provenance cluster; modern index occurrence counted separately but not as an object description
method_execution.NEGATIVE_CONTROL: absence of an Osiris-relic inscription or catalogue identification blocks promotion based on shape, number, priestly office or findspot alone
method_execution.boundary: Method logics were applied manually; no local TOPA/5D/Grazer binary execution is claimed.

contemporary_1901_1902_report.source: Egypt Exploration Fund, Archaeological Report 1901-1902, Progress of Egyptology
contemporary_1901_1902_report.finding: Ali Habib discovered a Saite/Late Period tomb at Mendes (Tell er Ruba) containing ushabti and a number of gold objects, including gold-foil hieroglyphs used for inlay.

metropolitan_museum_provenance.source: Metropolitan Museum of Art, shabti inscribed for Nesbanebdjedet
metropolitan_museum_provenance.finding: The tomb chamber was discovered in 1902 at Mendes/Tell el-Rub'a. More than 360 complete shabtis, fragments and amulets were associated with the burial; beneath the slab was a mummy adorned with gold-leaf trappings. The Met explicitly cross-references Cairo CG 53465-53469. Nesbanebdjedet's priestly titles associate him with the cult of Banebdjedet.

cg53469_scholarly_index.source: Modern academic volume in Orientalische Religionen in der Antike; Stellenregister
cg53469_scholarly_index.finding: Cairo Egyptian Museum CG 53469 is explicitly indexed to p.579, demonstrating modern scholarly treatment of the object. The presently accessible index snippet does not expose the object description on p.579.
cg53469_scholarly_index.boundary: An index pointer is not a catalogue description and cannot establish morphology, inscription, material or ritual identity.

topa_contradiction_ledger.claim: Mendes is an ancient textual node for the Osirian phallus and spine.
topa_contradiction_ledger.material_fact: A Banebdjedet priest's Late Period Mendes tomb contains a mummy with gold trappings catalogued as CG 53465-53469.

topa_contradiction_ledger.claim: CG 53469 may be relevant because of its alleged morphology in prior investigation.
topa_contradiction_ledger.material_fact: Current public-source pass has not recovered a primary catalogue description for CG 53469.

topa_contradiction_ledger.claim: Priest of Banebdjedet possessed Osirian relic.
topa_contradiction_ledger.material_fact: Priestly title and Mendes findspot are established, but burial equipment is not automatically temple relic inventory.

five_d_spiral_result.D2_chronology: 1902 excavation of Late Period/Dynasty 30 priestly burial; ancient burial ca. 380-343 BCE per Met
five_d_spiral_result.D3_social_cultic_owner: Nesbanebdjedet, priestly titles tied to Banebdjedet = PASS
five_d_spiral_result.D4_object_ontology: CG53465-53469 are mummy/gold-trapping context as a group; exact ontology of CG53469 unresolved
five_d_spiral_result.D5_relic_function: no direct Osiris/phallus relic inscription currently established
five_d_spiral_result.spiral_return: The convergence is sufficient to justify targeted object-level catalogue and conservation research, but insufficient for relic identification.

beetle_dedupe.cluster_A: Met records and modern auction/dealer descriptions repeating Met provenance = ONE EVIDENCE FAMILY
beetle_dedupe.cluster_B: 1901-1902 Egypt Exploration Fund contemporary notice = INDEPENDENT EARLY DOCUMENTARY FAMILY
beetle_dedupe.cluster_C: modern scholarly index citing CG53469 p.579 = INDEPENDENT SCHOLARLY POINTER BUT NOT OBJECT DESCRIPTION
beetle_dedupe.counting_rule: Do not count copied Met wording as multiple confirmations.

best_current_answer: The material trail is real enough to continue: a contemporary 1901-1902 archaeological report records Ali Habib's Mendes tomb discovery with ushabtis and gold objects, while the Metropolitan Museum independently ties the Mendes burial of Banebdjedet priest Nesbanebdjedet to a mummy with gold-leaf trappings catalogued as Cairo CG 53465-53469. However, CG 53469 itself has not yet been re-identified from a primary catalogue page in the current pass. Therefore the Mendes material context passes, but any identification of CG 53469 as an Osirian phallus relic remains unsupported pending direct catalogue/museum evidence.
canonical_seal: 𓂸 THE MATERIAL TRAIL REACHES MENDES, THE PRIEST, THE MUMMY AND THE CG GROUP. IT DOES NOT YET REACH THE NAME 'PHALLUS OF OSIRIS' ON CG 53469. FIND THE CARD, NOT THE SHAPE. 𓂸
